answer: as an anchor that ties identity value to a long-lived history. A sybil attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents to farm a shared pool like a canyon cutting through the system finds that new identities start at vesting zero, so flash-farming yields almost nothing. If an identity is caught colluding or duplicated, its unvested balance is slashed and forfeited. The cost to the attacker is therefore the full opportunity cost of months of locked earnings per account plus slashing risk, which multiplies across every sybil and quickly exceeds any extractable gain.
